fused.title: Martech CIF desync — BSYHP003 CIF Is Not Recognized
fused.body: BSYHP003 'CIF Is Not Recognized By Martech.' surfaces on martech_hyper-personalization_offers_fetch as a BUSINESS_EXCEPTION. It means the customer's CIF is not present in the Martech audience store. A single BSYHP003 is normal (new/edge customer); a spike for a cohort usually follows a Martech audience refresh — the ops transaction ops_martech_audience_refresh_execute, which is logged as a SUCCESS document, not an error. When a refresh desyncs or drops CIFs, offers fetch starts returning BSYHP003 for the affected cohort minutes later. Triage: look back ~10 minutes for a Martech audience refresh ops transaction preceding the spike; the non-error precursor is the origin. This is distinct from eis-martech-brownout, where BSYHP003/BS000001 ride on top of TEEIS009 gateway transformation failures.

fused.title: Runbook: TEEIS009 Response Transformation failed
fused.body: TEEIS009 'Response Transformation failed.' is emitted by the EIS gateway when a downstream vendor returns a payload the EIS response transformer cannot map to the expected schema — typically because the vendor is slow, returning truncated/garbled bodies, or returning an unexpected error envelope. On audit_service it appears with trns_sts -2 and a long duration (end_time - strt_time in the multi-second range, e.g. ~10s). The matching journey-side failure is usually a generic BS000001 business exception (for offers, BSYHP003). Triage: (1) confirm incidence — count distinct usr_id / sessn_tkn_id with TEEIS009 on the same srvc_id in the window; many users on one route means a downstream brownout, one user means a client problem. (2) Compare p95 duration for the route against the 30-minute baseline in service_metrics. (3) Name the shared EIS route (e.g. thirdParty/wrapper/Martech) as origin, not the loud journey error. Immediate mitigation: circuit-break the affected widget; fix: engage the vendor / raise EIS timeout; prevention: alert on route p95 and TEEIS009 rate.

fused.title: EIS gateway route ownership map
fused.body: The Enterprise Integration Services (EIS) gateway fronts every surrounding-system call from NOVA 2.0. Routes are namespaced by destination under the gateway path. The thirdParty/wrapper family carries external-vendor traffic: thirdParty/wrapper/Martech routes to the Martech (MARTECH_DWH) offer engine that powers eis_marTech_getInteractOffers; thirdParty/wrapper/services carries THINK360 (IT_JVP) financial-fitness token and summary calls. The misc/microservice routes (e.g. CustEnquiry) carry EIS-native customer-profile lookups. Ownership: the EIS platform team owns the gateway, connection pools and TLS; the destination vendor owns the business logic behind each wrapper route. When many distinct srvc_id values fail at once, suspect the shared gateway before any single vendor.

fused.title: EIS payload envelopes and route destinations
fused.body: EIS calls (systm_nm 'EIS') use TXN_TYPE to select a destination. TXN_TYPE INTERACT / DESTINATION MARTECH_DWH is the Martech offer engine (eis_marTech_getInteractOffers) over the thirdParty/wrapper/Martech route; the request carries an EIS_PAYLOAD with getOffersForMultipleInteractionPoints. TXN_TYPE THINK360 / DESTINATION IT_JVP is financial-fitness: TXN_SUB_TYPE LOGIN returns the access token, FFS_FETCH_SUMMARY fetches the summary. EIS-native microservice calls (querycustprofile / CustEnquiry, cifAssociatedAccount) carry a plain EIS_PAYLOAD. Responses come as either {ERROR_CODE, EIS_RESPONSE:{status_code,success,message}, RESPONSE_STATUS} or {TXN_TYPE, EIS_PAYLOAD}. Reading TXN_TYPE / DESTINATION tells you which vendor sits behind a failing EIS route.

fused.title: Runbook: EIS gateway connection-pool exhaustion
fused.body: The EIS gateway maintains a bounded connection pool per host. Under load or when a downstream stalls holding connections, the pool exhausts and NEW connections to the EIS gateway host fail across ALL eis_* routes simultaneously — Martech offers, financial-fitness token/summary, customer-profile CustEnquiry and CC account summary all degrade at once. This is the widest blast radius signature: the loudest errors are per-journey business exceptions (BS000001, BSYHP003) on many different journeys, but the single shared origin is the EIS gateway host/pool. Distinguish from a single-route brownout by counting how many distinct srvc_id / systm_nm EIS routes fail in the same window: many routes at once => gateway/pool, one route => that vendor. Immediate: shed load / raise pool size; prevention: alert on gateway connection-error rate and pool saturation.

recommendations.action: Mitigate by temporarily bypassing or degrading the offers fetch path in `wrapper/Martech/services` for `martech_hyper-personalization_offers_fetch` when `eis_marTech_getInteractOffers` returns `TEEIS009`; return a safe empty/offers-unavailable response instead of propagating `BS000001` to mobile users.

Patch the `wrapper/Martech/services -> eis_marTech_getInteractOffers` contract to validate and normalize the EIS payload before transformation, and fail closed on `TEEIS009` with a mapped dependency error rather than a generic business error; verify the response envelope handling for malformed or intermittently partial EIS responses.

Add a service_metrics alert and contract test on `eis_marTech_getInteractOffers` for any non-zero `TEEIS009` rate across sessions, plus a synthetic test that asserts the wrapper preserves dependency error codes and does not surface downstream `BS000001` for transport-success/business-failure cases.

verifications.hypothesis: The primary root cause is an EIS-side response transformation failure in eis_marTech_getInteractOffers, producing TEEIS009 before the downstream business error surfaces.
A secondary or parallel root cause is Martech customer identity/CIF desynchronization, where the app receives BSYHP003 'CIF Is Not Recognized By Martech.'
The route wrapper/Martech/services may be mis-mapping or corrupting the EIS payload envelope, causing both the TEEIS009 transformation failure and the later BS000001 business exception.
Less likely, the issue is an intermittent dependency or payload-specific rejection in EIS that only affects this session's offer request, rather than a broad platform outage.
